post.title: Color in a Jar, Volume One
post.body:
This is Volume One of Color in a Jar: coloring pages where every scene lives inside glass.

The first jar holds a walled garden. A plum tree leans over an iron gate that stands open, a cobbled path runs back past an ivy-covered wall, and a stone tower sits at the far end. The next is shallower, a round glass dish turned into a pond, with water lilies, a willow hanging over it and a dragonfly resting on a reed.

Then the scenes go farther afield. A snowy village sits in a jar tagged Alpine Adventure, with a lit-up tree in the square, skaters on a frozen pond and mountains under a crescent moon. There's a savanna with a lion resting under an acacia and a giraffe walking past a big low sun. There's a bamboo grove around a stone lantern, a forest floor under a bell jar with spotted mushrooms, curled fern fronds and a snail, and a glass greenhouse dome full of orchids and palms with butterflies on the outside.

The desert gets its turn too: a bowl of succulents with a string of pearls spilling over the rim and a lizard on a rock, and a jar holding an oasis, a pool between palms with a camel resting beside it.

One page shows up three ways. The message in a bottle, with its little island, hammock, campfire, treasure chest and parrots, is here as clean line art and also colored in, so you can see where the page can go. And the same island appears as a full scene: a brass robot and a robot dog in a pirate hat at the treasure chest, and a mermaid in the shallows watching.

The jar is the frame. Every page gets a clear edge, and inside it, the whole world can be as busy as you like.

episode.title: Worlds in a jar
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

This Note came without a trail, a tracker or a single mile. It came in a jar.

Color in a Jar, Volume One, is a set of coloring pages, and every one of them puts a whole world behind glass.

The first holds a garden. A plum tree heavy with fruit, an iron gate standing open, a cobbled path that winds back toward an old stone tower. The next is barely a jar at all, more of a shallow glass dish, with water lilies, a willow bending over the water and a dragonfly resting on a reed.

***

After that, the jars start to travel. A snowy village with skaters on a frozen pond, and a little tag on the lid that says Alpine Adventure. A lion resting in the shade of an acacia while a giraffe strolls past a low, enormous sun. A bamboo grove around a stone lantern. Spotted mushrooms and curled ferns under a bell jar, with a snail making its slow way up a branch.

The high desert gets a page or two as well. A bowl of succulents with a lizard keeping watch on a rock. An oasis in a jar, where a camel has found the one patch of shade and decided to stay.

***

Then there's the bottle. A message in a bottle, lying in the sand, with an island inside: palm trees, a hammock, a campfire and a treasure chest. It appears as plain lines, then colored in, all blue water and green palms. And then it appears as a full scene, where a brass robot and a robot dog in a pirate hat are opening that chest, and a mermaid watches from the shallows.

The brass robot looks a little familiar. I'll say no more than that.

What I like about the set is the frame. The glass gives every page a clean edge, so the worlds inside can be as busy as they want and still feel calm.

***

This one's called Volume One. Jars, after all, are made to be filled.
